A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same iQUEST study. The main text, figures, tables, equations, algorithm, and Appendices A–E support a complete comparison; the shorter pagination in v4 does not reflect missing content.

before.justification: V3 reports original iQUEST benchmark results, component ablations, runtime measurements, and missing-entity error analyses in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark and ablation results in Tables 1–6 and runtime and error-analysis results in Tables 7–9.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same iterative question guidance, two-hop GNN entity selection, answer extraction, context updates, and stopping procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use CWQ, WebQSP, WebQuestions, and GrailQA over Freebase, including the same generalization evaluation and one-, two-, and three-hop runtime scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Question-Decomposition, Chain-of-Question, KG-CoT, FlexKBQA, Interactive-KBQA, and ToG. The ablation comparators and ToG comparisons in Appendix B are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain Hit@1 evaluation, the 1,000-instance GrailQA sampling strategy, and the same model configurations. Appendix B retains 100 sampled questions per hop category, GPT-4o via Azure OpenAI, and the correct-chain-only runtime control.

E4.justification: The KG, GNN, IQG-LLM, and AE-LLM ablations are unchanged. Appendices B–E retain the controlled runtime analysis, missing-fact discussion, missing-entity analysis, and Forrest Gump failure case.

E5.justification: Both retain the same point-estimate and average-runtime reporting. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Corresponding numerical entries and reported findings in Tables 1–9 are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains iQUEST scores of 73.85, 88.93, 81.23, and 73.52 for CWQ, WebQSP, WebQuestions, and GrailQA, respectively.

T1.justification: The KG and KBQA definitions, Equations 1–5, and assumptions in Section 5.2.1 are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical revision is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: iterative question guidance, two-hop GNN lookahead, and effectiveness across four datasets and four LLMs. Abstract wording changes do not alter claim scope.

C2.justification: Both retain the same interpretations of reasoning versus internal knowledge, GNN retrieval benefits, and runtime tradeoffs. Limitations concerning computational overhead, two-hop scope, incomplete KGs, and repetitive or drifting sub-questions are unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain identical, including model versions, BERT encoding with dimension 768, GNN hidden dimension 128, top-3 retrieval, and random negative sampling. No implementation or resource-access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, and positioning against existing KBQA, question-decomposition, and entity-exploration approaches are unchanged.

P1.justification: V4 removes the 'iQUEST:' prefix from the title and lightly rewrites the abstract's opening and transition wording. The remaining prose and section sequence are unchanged apart from reflow.

P2.justification: V4 places Table 6 before Appendix B and groups runtime Tables 7–8 together. Appendix E now fits on one page. Figures, table structures, and captions are unchanged; these are limited placement and pagination changes.

improvement.justification: V4 modestly improves appendix readability by placing Table 6 immediately after Appendix A, grouping the runtime tables, and keeping the failure case and its interpretation together. The benefit is presentational; methods, evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged.
